title: The Words — Sc061: Darwin peeks and points around the layout-video giant (100 frames)

source.github: mhvnsnt/cn-gigaleak-gumball, draft release untagged-1676e192ae8c72e95791, asset id 640772406
source.method: FLA (XFL zip) read via sequential local-header parser (2012 Flash zips have malformed central directory); DOMDocument.xml + LIBRARY symbol XMLs parsed directly. Same neutral per-keyframe transform format as production/dance-choreo v1: a part pose is (item, first_frame, affine matrix a/b/c/d/tx/ty, pivot). keyMode 9728 = pose-to-pose; sampled_frames hold each keyframe's elements to the next keyframe, matching SWF playback.

teaches: A Flash scene can be only half of the finished shot. Sc061's only puppet is Darwin (279 kf, with 2,415 kf of face comps), but the frame is dominated by a giant classmate who is not in the Flash file at all as artwork - she is a DOMVideoInstance on the 'layout mov' layer, a separately produced (3D-style) character embedded as reference so the Flash animator can puppeteer Darwin around her exact head positions: peeking right, peeking left, then stepping out front to point at her. The lesson for any mixed-pipeline production: animate the in-file character against the other pipeline's render, in the same file, frame-matched - never guess the composite positions later. The file also shows the failure mode to avoid: its fieldguide layer was left as a regular layer, so the safe-area guides render into the export.
notes: FILE-EVIDENCE SURPRISE: the Flash puppet cast is Darwin only, but the rendered frames are dominated by a giant horned, long-haired, clawed classmate who exists ONLY as a DOMVideoInstance on the 'layout mov' layer - a separately produced character (3D-style) carried in the file as reference video for compositing. She is unnamed anywhere in the FLA.

Darwin's puppet performance is choreographed against that video: he peeks from behind her head - right side grinning (f13), open-mouth (f26), laughing (f38), then left side (f51-63) - and finally steps out front at f75-100, pointing up at her and then at her face with shocked/arguing expressions.

This file's fieldguide layer is NOT typed as a guide (3 keyframes, regular layer), so the production safe-area overlay (red 14:9/16:9 safe marks) renders visibly in the exported frames - unlike the other scenes in this batch, where the fieldguide is a hidden guide layer.

Background is again GB214_WORDS_SC057_LO_BG_crop.jpg, almost entirely occluded by the reference-video character; no photo-plate tag is claimed for this scene because the plate is barely visible in the render.
